description: Exact all-occurrences search using Reverse Factor with a turbo remembered-prefix reinspection rule.

source.title: Speeding up two string-matching algorithms
source.algorithm_description: ESMAJ Chapter 26, Turbo Reverse Factor algorithm
source.source_license: Copyright belongs to cited authors and publishers. Mathematical algorithm descriptions only; independent implementation and workload.

workspace.meaning: Pattern staging and Morris–Pratt border table, plus a fixed dense suffix automaton with transition destinations, transition displacements, suffix links, state lengths, representative positions, and terminal flags. Text is read from the validated input frame.

contract.automaton: Build a suffix automaton for the reversed pattern. Each defined transition stores a destination and displacement; suffix links, maximum state lengths, representative positions, and terminal states are retained.
contract.border_table: For each prefix length k, mp_next[k] is the length of its longest proper border, with mp_next[0]=-1; the pattern period is m-mp_next[m].
contract.window_scan: Scan each candidate window from right to left through the reversed-pattern suffix automaton, accumulating transition displacement and retaining the rightmost terminal-state shift.
contract.turbo_reinspection: Remember the preceding shift. After matching the new right-hand factor, re-inspect only min(period(prefix), floor(prefix_length/2)) characters for a periodic prefix, or the appropriate right half for a nonperiodic prefix.
contract.occurrences: A zero accumulated displacement after scanning through the remembered-prefix boundary reports the current start; shift by the pattern period to retain overlaps.
contract.complexity: O(m) preprocessing and O(n) search; the published algorithm performs at most 2n text character inspections.
contract.state_bound: Two sentinel states plus at most 2*m pattern-derived states fit in the 2*m+2=258 state allocation.
contract.workspace_bound: Two 258-by-4 i64 transition tables, three 258-entry i64 state tables, one 258-entry i64 terminal table, a 128-entry i64 pattern, a 129-entry i64 MP table, and scalar state fit within 28672 bytes.
contract.result_bounds: At most 4096 matches and the sum of offsets is below 2^23, so the packed result is below 2^49 and fits signed 64-bit.
contract.error_precedence: Validate input pointer, parseable length, header, exact packed length, and symbol ranges before preprocessing.
